prompt.text_original: A present-day country the Euphrates flows through
prompt.citation: Genesis 15:18; Revelation 9:14
prompt.summary: The Euphrates is one of the great rivers of the Bible. When the Lord made a covenant with Abram, He named the Euphrates as a boundary of the land given to his seed (Genesis 15:18). The river rises in eastern Turkey, crosses Syria past ancient Carchemish and Mari, and flows through Iraq past Babylon and Ur.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The Euphrates passes ancient Babylon and Ur in Iraq.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: The river crosses eastern Syria past Carchemish and Mari.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: The Euphrates rises in the highlands of eastern Turkey.

prompt.text_original: A present-day country where an ancient inscription naming a king of Israel or Judah was found
prompt.citation: Archaeology: Mesha Stele, Tel Dan, Kurkh, Black Obelisk
prompt.summary: Archaeologists have found ancient stone monuments that name kings from the Bible. The Mesha Stele from Jordan names Omri of Israel, the Kurkh Monolith from Turkey names Ahab, and the Black Obelisk from Iraq shows Jehu, while Sennacherib's prisms name Hezekiah. The Tel Dan stele, found in Israel, mentions the House of David.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The Tel Dan stele mentions the 'House of David'.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The Black Obelisk from Nimrud shows Jehu, and Sennacherib's prisms name Hezekiah.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: The Mesha Stele, found at Dhiban, names Omri of Israel.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: The Kurkh Monolith, found near Diyarbakir, names Ahab.

prompt.text_original: A present-day country with a Philistine or Phoenician city named in the Old Testament
prompt.citation: 1 Samuel 5-6; 1 Kings 5; Ezekiel 27
prompt.summary: The Philistines lived along the southern coast in cities like Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron and Gath, now in Israel, and they were often at war with Israel. To the north, the Phoenicians built cities such as Tyre, Sidon, Gebal (Byblos) and the island city of Arvad, today's Arwad off Syria (Ezekiel 27:8).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron and Gath were Philistine cities now in Israel.

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Tyre, Sidon and Gebal (Byblos) were Phoenician.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Arvad, Phoenician island-city Arwad, is off Syria (Ezekiel 27:8).

prompt.text_original: A country that hosted one of the Church's first four area general conferences (1971 to 1974).
prompt.citation: Ensign, Nov. 1974, "Making Conferences Turning Points in Our Lives"; Ensign, Dec. 1973, Stockholm announcement
prompt.summary: In the early 1970s the Church began holding area general conferences so Saints who could not travel to Salt Lake City could be taught by Church leaders close to home. The first was in Manchester, England, in 1971, followed by Mexico City (1972) and Munich (1973). The fourth, in Stockholm in August 1974, was for members in Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Manchester, England, 1971, the first area conference.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Stockholm, August 1974, for Scandinavian and Finnish Saints.

prompt.summary: Nicolai Dorius was a Danish convert who emigrated to Utah in 1855. His wagon train of nearly 400 Saints from Denmark, Norway, England and Nova Scotia left Mormon Grove, a prairie camp about a thousand miles east of the Salt Lake Valley, on June 13, 1855. Two of his daughters died on the journey, and the company reached the valley in early September.

prompt.text_original: A country containing a land Abraham lives in or travels through in the Book of Abraham (Chaldea, Haran, Canaan, Egypt)

prompt.summary: In the Book of Abraham, a famine strikes Ur of the Chaldees and the Lord tells Abraham to leave for a land He will show him (Abraham 2:1-4). Abraham stays for a time in Haran, then at age 62 travels on to Canaan, where the Lord promises the land to his descendants (Abraham 2:14-19). When famine continues, he goes down into Egypt (Abraham 2:21).

answers.name: Egypt

answers.name: Iraq

answers.name: Israel

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Haran, where Abraham's family settled (Abraham 2:4), is identified with Harran in southeastern Turkey.

prompt.text_original: A country tied to the Joseph Smith papyri: where they were dug up, the excavator's homeland, or where Joseph Smith acquired them
prompt.citation: Gospel Topics essay, Translation and Historicity of the Book of Abraham
prompt.summary: Antonio Lebolo, a former Italian cavalryman, took 11 mummies from a tomb near ancient Thebes in Egypt. In 1835 Saints in Kirtland, Ohio, bought the remaining mummies and papyrus scrolls, and Joseph Smith worked on a translation that became the Book of Abraham. Most of the papyri were likely lost in the 1871 Chicago fire, but New York's Metropolitan Museum gave surviving fragments to the Church in 1967.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Antonio Lebolo took 11 mummies from a tomb near ancient Thebes.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Saints in Kirtland, Ohio, bought the mummies and scrolls in 1835; New York's Metropolitan Museum gave fragments to the Church in 1967.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Lebolo was a former cavalryman in the Italian army working for the French consul general.

answers.name: Egypt

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The Jordan River, which Israel crossed (1 Nephi 17:32), forms in northern Israel and flows to the Sea of Galilee.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: The Jordan River crossing in 1 Nephi 17:32 is on the river from which Jordan takes its name.
